chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Zayd al-Shahham who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Indeed, God (Blessed and Exalted) took Ibrahim as a servant before He took him as a Prophet, and indeed God took him as a Prophet before He took him as a Messenger, and indeed God took him as a Messenger before He took him as a close friend (Khalil), and indeed God took him as a close friend before He made him an Imam.

So when He had gathered all these things for him, He said: [2:124] 'Indeed, I am making you an Imam for the people.' He (the Imam) said: And it was due to its greatness in the eyes of Ibrahim that he said: 'And from my offspring?' He said: [2:124] 'My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.'
He (the Imam) said: 'The foolish one cannot be the Imam of the pious.'

key_terms.إمام: Imam — the highest station of divinely appointed leadership over all humanity
key_terms.تقي: Pious one — the God-fearing believer whom the Imam serves
key_terms.خليل: Close friend/beloved — Abraham's special title (Khalilullah, Friend of God) referenced in Quran 4:125
key_terms.رسول: Messenger (Rasul) — a prophet sent with a universal mission and scripture
key_terms.سفيه: Foolish/ignorant one — one lacking the moral and intellectual qualifications for leadership
key_terms.عبد: Servant — the foundational station of total submission to God, prerequisite to all higher stations
key_terms.عهد: Covenant — the divine trust and appointment that cannot reach the unjust
key_terms.نبي: Prophet (Nabi) — one who receives divine revelation

ai.seo_question: What is the hierarchy of Ibrahim's divine stations according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) expounds the hierarchical progression of Ibrahim's (AS) divine stations: servanthood, prophethood, messengership, close friendship (khullah), and finally imamate—each conferred only after the previous was perfected. The climax is the divine declaration from Quran 2:124, which the Imam then interprets with the principle that the wrongdoer cannot attain the covenant of imamate. This hadith establishes imamate as the highest station, surpassing even prophethood and messengership, and affirms that it cannot be held by the unjust—a foundational Shia theological argument against the legitimacy of unjust rulers.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Zayd Al Shahham who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Took Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> as a servant before He<sup>azwj</sup> Took him<sup>as</sup> as a Prophet<sup>as</sup>, and that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Took him<sup>as</sup> as a Prophet before He<sup>azwj</sup> Took him<sup>as</sup> as a Rasool<sup>as</sup>, and that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Took him<sup>as</sup> as a Rasool<sup>as</sup> before He<sup>azwj</sup> Took him<sup>as</sup> as a friend, and that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Took him<sup>as</sup> as a friend before He<sup>azwj</sup> Took him<sup>as</sup> as an Imam.

So when the things were gathered for himas, Heazwj Said [2:124] I Make you to be an Imam of the people. So it was a great matter in the eyes of Ibrahimas, so heas said [2:124] Ibrahim said: And from my offspring? He Said: My Covenant cannot be attained by the unjust’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The foolish cannot happen to be an Imam of the pious’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan has narrated those whom he mentioned from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Zayd al-Shahham who has said the following. “I heard Imam abu ‘Abdallah saying, ‘

Allah chose Abraham as a servant before choosing him as a prophet. Allah chose him as a prophet before choosing him as a messenger. Allah chose him as a messenger before choosing him as a friend of His. Allah chose him as a friend of His before choosing him as an Imam. When all of the above things were gathered in Abraham, Allah said, “I have certainly appointed you as the Imam for the people.” Because to Abraham it was so great he asked, “Can this (Imamat, leadership) be in my descendents also?”
The feeble-minded can become the leaders of the pious ones.”
